news.title: D & H India Limited announced that it expects to receive INR 81.42675 million in funding
news.body: D & H India Limited announced a private placement of up to 2,157,000 convertible warrants at a price of INR 37.75 per warrant for gross proceeds of up to INR 81,426,750 on March 14, 2026. Each warrant convertible into 21,57,000 equity shares of INR10/- at premium in one or more tranches within a period of 18 months from the date of allotment of warrants on preferential basis to promoters and promoter group of the company. The transaction involves new investor participation of Shri Harsh Vora for 6,15,000 warrants, Shri Saurabh Vora for 7,86,000 warrants, Smt. Kiran Vora for 7,56,000 warrants. The transaction has been approved by the board of directors and subject to approval of members in their Extra Ordinary General Meeting scheduled to be held on April 10, 2026.

news.title: New minor risk - Shareholder dilution
news.body: The company's shareholders have been diluted in the past year. Increase in shares outstanding: 25% This is considered a minor risk. Shareholder dilution occurs when there is an increase in the number of shares on issue that is not proportionally distributed between all shareholders. Often due to the company raising equity capital or some options being converted into stock. All else being equal, if there are more shares outstanding then each existing share will be entitled to a lower proportion of the company's total earnings, thus reducing earnings per share (EPS). news.body: Third quarter 2026 results: EPS: ₹2.64 (up from ₹1.90 in 3Q 2025). Revenue: ₹621.2m (up 13% from 3Q 2025). Net income: ₹24.3m (up 44% from 3Q 2025). Profit margin: 3.9% (up from 3.1% in 3Q 2025). The increase in margin was driven by higher revenue. Over the last 3 years on average, earnings per share has increased by 17% per year but the company’s share price has increased by 36% per year, which means it is tracking significantly ahead of earnings growth.
